text: **Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) represent the state-of-the-art paradigm in mechanistic interpretability for LLMs, focusing on decomposing superimposed activations into monosemantic features.**[1](https://arxiv.org/html/2406.04093v1)[2](https://cdn.openai.com/papers/sparse-autoencoders.pdf)

Key metrics are reconstruction-focused (MSE, explained variance/R², loss recovery), sparsity (L0 norm 50-150, dead latents <1-5%), monosemanticity (FMS, MS score via Jensen-Shannon distance, auto-interpretability F1), and downstream (sparse probing accuracy, MCC, feature uniqueness, CPR/CMD for circuits).[8](https://arxiv.org/html/2506.19382v1)[9](https://arxiv.org/html/2503.09532v3)[10](https://arxiv.org/html/2504.02821v3)[6](https://arxiv.org/html/2602.14687v1)[11](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.1

SOTA SAEs achieve MSE scaling as L(N,K) ≈ 0.1-0.5 (joint n latents, k sparsity on GPT-4), >90-95% loss recovery, R² >0.9, dead latents <1%, auto-interp F1 0.4-0.7, sparse probing 70-90% on tasks; G-SAEs double monosemanticity vs. vanilla. Domain-specific SAEs boost variance explained and clinical F1 vs. broad-domain.[12](https://www.perplexity.ai/search/7412d7a1-e7cc-485a-8095-57eb69490d3b)[13](https://huggingface.co/papers/2506.19382)[14](https://arxiv.org/html/2508.09363v1)[9](https://arxiv.or

Dominant setups use overcomplete (4-128x expansion, millions latents) encoder-decoder with L1/TopK sparsity, JumpReLU/ProLu activation; variants include Gated/TopK/BatchTopK/LayerGroup/Switch/Matryoshka SAEs for better scaling/steering. Trained via TransformerLens/SAELens/Sparsify on residual streams; shift to domain-specific training and automated circuit discovery.[15](https://www.taskade.com/blog/what-is-mechanistic-interpretability)[16](https://www.emergentmind.com/topics/sparse-autoencoder-

- **Dead latents and sparsity tuning**: Even SOTA k-sparse/TopK variants yield 1-5% dead latents; no robust theory predicts optimal hyperparameters across model scales.[7](https://proceedings.iclr.cc/paper_files/paper/2025/file/42ef3308c230942d223c411adf182c88-Paper-Conference.pdf)[6](https://arxiv.org/html/2406.04093v1)
- Vanilla L1-SAE (SAELens default): Expansion factor 8-16x, on Pythia-70M/GPT2-small residuals.[5](https://github.com/jbloomAus/SAELens)

Our findings on auxiliary logit-steering losses for Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) directly address pathological reconstruction errors documented in prior work, where low-MSE outputs amplify KL-divergence in next-token predictions by 2-4x over random noise of equivalent L2 norm. We demonstrate that a simple auxiliary logit-steering loss mitigates pathological reconstruction errors in Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs), reducing KL-divergence amplification by 25-40% against L2-matched baselines while preserving >90% recovery, L0 sparsity near 100, and downstream sparse probing gains of 4-7% AUROC on SAEBench—all on accessible Pythia-1.4B/Gemma-2B residuals.
